for Loop Number Check

Source: R/for_loop_nb_check.R
for_loop_nb_check.Rd

Check the sequence expression of every for loop of a function. If the number of iterations is not fixed by the writing itself (e.g., 1:length(x)), a checking line is added before the loop, issuing a warning at execution if the sequence is empty, contains NA or infinite values, has a single value, or is decreasing. Return a table-like message of the problematic lines and a corrected version of the submitted function.

Usage

for_loop_nb_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

A function name, written without quotes and brackets.

export

Single logical value. Write the corrected function into a file instead of returning it? If TRUE, the file <function name>_safer.R is written in out_path (e.g., fun_safer.R for x = fun or x = pkg::fun). It contains fun_safer <- function(...) ..., so that base::source() recreates the corrected function. Nothing is written if nothing has to be corrected. An error is returned if the file already exists, or if x is not a function name (e.g., function(x){x} or FUN_LIST$fun).

out_path

Single character string indicating the path of the folder where to write the file when export = TRUE. "." (default) means the R working directory. Ignored if export = FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A table-like message is always printed, with one row per reported loop (column 1: line number; column 2: construct; column 3: code before the body), or a message saying that everything seems fine.

If export = FALSE: the corrected function, or NULL if nothing has been corrected.

If export = TRUE: NULL, returned invisibly. The corrected function is written in a file (see the export argument).

Details

Not reported: hard numbers, i.e., an integer-valued number, possibly negative, or two such numbers joined by : (e.g., 3, 1:3, 1e3, 1L:3L, 0:0, -3:-1, 1:0), and a single seq_len(...) or seq_along(...) call. These writings fully fix the iterations, and their control is left to the writer.

Reported: everything else, e.g., for(i in x), 1:n, 1:length(x), 1:nrow(df), 1:(n - 1), seq_along(x) - 1, 1:2.5, 1:NA or 1:Inf. Comments and strings are ignored.

Why: with x <- character(), for(i in 1:length(x)) runs twice, because 1:length(x) is c(1, 0). Use base::seq_along(along.with = x) instead.

Correction: each reported loop becomes tempo_for_seqN <- <SEQUENCE> ; <CHECKS> ; for(i in tempo_for_seqN)<BODY>, N being the rank of the report. The checks warn if the sequence is empty, contains NA or infinite values, has a single value, has only negative values, or is decreasing (these last two checks only for numeric sequences, i.e., not for factors, dates, characters or complex numbers). The loop thus runs on the checked sequence. Errors of the sequence itself (like 1:NA) are not caught. If the loop is not a standalone statement (e.g., unbraced body of an if, or argument value), the whole is enclosed in curly brackets. The rest of the code is unchanged. The comments are kept in the exported file, but can be lost in the returned function. The returned function is evaluated in a new environment whose parent is the environment of the submitted function: check it before replacing the original function.

Warning: a reported loop is left unchanged, and listed in the message, when:

  • the name tempo_for_seqN is already used in the function code (including comments and strings);

  • the loop is inside the sequence expression of another reported loop;

  • the loop must be enclosed in curly brackets and contains comments;

  • the loop must be enclosed in curly brackets and ends with another loop that must also be (e.g., for(a in 1:n) for(b in 1:length(x)){...}).

Warning: only the writing is analyzed. In n <- length(x) ; for(i in 1:n), 1:n is reported as a variable, whatever n.

Line numbers are indicative. They start at the <- function line (#' header lines not counted). Compiled functions, like saferDev::colons_check, have no comments: their line numbers differ from their source file.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/for_loop_nb_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ for(i in base::seq_along(along.with = x)){ base::print(x = i) } }
saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun1) # everything fine: NULL returned
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
fun2 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:length(x)){ base::print(x = i) } }
fun2_safer <- saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun2) # 1:length(x) reported
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED FUNCTION RETURNED BY return().
#> 
fun2_safer # corrected function
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     tempo_for_seq1 <- 1:length(x)
#>     if (base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) == 0) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE EMPTY: 0 ITERATION", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::anyNA(x = tempo_for_seq1)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH NA VALUES", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) == 1) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH A SINGLE VALUE (EQUAL BOUNDS?): SINGLE ITERATION", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::any(base::is.infinite(x = tempo_for_seq1), 
#>         na.rm = TRUE)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH INFINITE VALUES: NO ENDLESS LOOP POSSIBLE BECAUSE THE for() CONTROLLER IS FULLY EVALUATED BEFORE ITERATING, BUT CHECK THAT AN INFINITE VALUE IS EXPECTED", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.numeric(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::all(tempo_for_seq1 < 
#>         0, na.rm = FALSE)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH ALL NEGATIVE VALUES", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.numeric(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) >= 
#>         2 && tempo_for_seq1[1] > tempo_for_seq1[2]) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE DECREASING", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     for (i in tempo_for_seq1) {
#>         base::print(x = i)
#>     }
#> }
#> <environment: 0x55f9aa80c5a8>
fun2_safer(x = base::character()) # warning: 1:length(x) is c(1, 0), a decreasing sequence
#> Warning: FOR SEQUENCE DECREASING
#> [1] 1
#> [1] 0
# Write the corrected function in the fun2_safer.R file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun2, export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpvlxsPN/dir142ffda7714/fun2_safer.R
#>
